stories.body: Russia launched its heaviest combined assault on Ukrainian energy infrastructure in months, killing seven people and causing emergency power cuts in Kyiv and nearby regions. The attack intensified concerns about Ukraine’s ability to maintain power and heating through the winter, as Russia continues to target energy facilities while Ukraine faces shortages of air-defence missiles. The strikes came as President Vladimir Putin prepared to address the Valdai Discussion Club, with no indication that the Kremlin is preparing to halt its full-scale invasion.
stories.headline: Russia’s major strike on Ukraine’s energy grid kills seven and triggers emergency power cuts

stories.body: Pakistan said it struck camps and hideouts used by the Pakistani Taliban and the Balochistan Liberation Army in Afghanistan, reporting that 22 fighters were killed. Afghanistan’s Taliban government said the raids hit homes in Kunar and Helmand provinces, killing at least nine women and children and injuring 11 others. The competing claims could not be independently verified, but the attacks mark a renewed escalation after months of relative calm between the neighbouring countries.
stories.headline: Pakistan launches air raids in Afghanistan as Kabul reports civilian deaths

stories.body: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Israel, Oman and the United States are investigating after a Flydubai co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain of a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight and attempted to crash it. Israeli passengers reportedly helped restrain the co-pilot, while reserve crew members stabilised the aircraft after it plunged nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds and diverted it to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The captain and first officer were hospitalised, the motive remains unknown, and Flydubai has suspended flights to and from Israel pending the investigation.
stories.headline: International investigation opens after Flydubai co-pilot allegedly attacks captain on Israel-bound flight

stories.body: Christa Pike, Tennessee’s only woman on death row, was taken to hospital after two doses of pentobarbital failed to kill her during an execution attempt. Her lawyers said she lost consciousness but still had a heartbeat and was audibly snoring, while state officials said the execution protocol had been followed. Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent review of what happened and halted the state’s remaining execution scheduled for this year. Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer.
stories.headline: Tennessee death-row prisoner Christa Pike survives failed execution attempt

stories.body: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their remaining ice in the first eight months of 2026, bringing their total loss since 2021 to 19.4%, according to glacier-monitoring scientists. A winter with little snow followed by intense summer heatwaves exposed dark glacier ice that absorbed more solar heat and melted rapidly. Researchers warn that the retreat threatens long-term water supplies for farming, hydropower and river transport, while glacier thinning and thawing mountain ground can also increase the risk of landslides and flooding.
stories.headline: Swiss glaciers lose nearly a fifth of their ice in five years

stories.body: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon has removed 20% of its generals, admirals and other senior officers as part of a broader overhaul of the US military. In a speech at Marine Corps Base Quantico, he promoted what he called a warrior ethos, attacked diversity initiatives and announced plans including an Autonomous Warfare Command for robotics, drones and artificial intelligence. Critics have described the personnel changes as a purge; Hegseth said they were overdue accountability.
stories.headline: Trump administration says it has cut 20% of Pentagon generals and admirals

stories.body: Republican candidates are weighing President Donald Trump’s ability to energise core supporters against concerns that his weak approval ratings and association with high costs and the Iran war could alienate undecided voters. Some campaigns have reportedly urged Trump not to visit closely contested districts, while party strategists see him as essential to turning out lower-propensity voters who often skip midterms. The party is instead trying to direct Trump’s appearances toward areas where a boost in Republican turnout is likely to outweigh any loss of persuadable voters.
stories.headline: Republicans debate whether Trump will help or hurt them in competitive midterm races

stories.body: Fewer Democrats say they plan to vote by mail in the midterms than at the comparable point in 2024, as concerns about ballot security and postal delivery persist despite the Supreme Court blocking the Trump administration’s proposed restrictions. An NBC News poll found that 23% of registered Democrats plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in September 2024, while early in-person voting has increased. Election officials and advocacy groups are urging voters to make plans early, use ballot-tracking tools where available and return mailed ballots well ahead of deadlines.
stories.headline: Democrats reconsider mail-voting plans despite court protection for the system

stories.body: A bipartisan proposal in Congress would provide funding to states that adopt and enforce restrictions on student cellphone use in schools. The measure seeks to encourage a nationwide shift toward anti-cellphone policies, though its approval would be required before states could receive the proposed funding.
stories.headline: Bipartisan bill would encourage cellphone bans in schools nationwide

stories.body: Podemos said its four members of Congress will support the Spanish government’s two housing decrees after pressure from tenants’ organisations, despite continuing to call the measures inadequate. Its decision shifts attention to Junts and, to a lesser extent, the Basque Nationalist Party, whose votes could determine whether the measures are ratified. The government is considered more likely to secure approval for one decree than for the second, which concerns lease extensions and compensation mechanisms.
stories.headline: Spain’s housing decrees depend on Junts after Podemos backs them

stories.body: Spain’s meteorological agency issued its highest-level weather warnings for parts of Castellón, Valencia and Tarragona, forecasting up to 90 litres of rain per square metre in an hour and as much as 250 litres over 12 hours. Civil Protection sent emergency alerts to residents, advised them to avoid travel and waterways, and urged them to follow road closures. Dozens of Valencian municipalities suspended classes, while authorities warned that the rain could cause sudden flooding in ravines and smaller watercourses.
stories.headline: Spain issues red alerts for torrential rain in Castellón, Valencia and Tarragona

stories.body: The UN special rapporteur on torture called for a prompt, effective and independent investigation into allegations that Spanish military personnel abused migrants in Ceuta. The intervention followed an Amnesty International report and additional accounts from migrants who said soldiers beat them at night in areas where they were sleeping outdoors. The rapporteur said that, if confirmed, the allegations could amount to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment and in some cases torture.
stories.headline: UN torture expert calls for independent investigation into alleged abuse of migrants in Ceuta

stories.body: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia will visit Ceuta and Melilla on 13 and 14 October, the royal household and Spanish government announced. It will be Felipe’s first trip to the autonomous cities since becoming king in 2014 and the first royal visit there in nearly 20 years. The visit comes roughly two and a half months after a major migration crisis in Ceuta; Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will not accompany the royals.
stories.headline: Spain’s king and queen will visit Ceuta and Melilla on 13 and 14 October

stories.body: Barcelona activated its municipal emergency plan for drainage and flood risk as intense rain and storms were forecast, only a day after the previous alert was lifted. Catalan Civil Protection also activated the Inuncat plan, while weather warnings covered much of Catalonia and the greatest danger was expected in southern counties. Authorities sent mobile alerts in Tarragona, Penedès and Garraf, warning people to avoid flood-prone areas, rivers and smaller streams and to take extra care while travelling.
stories.headline: Barcelona activates flood alert as intense rain and storms approach

stories.body: Catalonia’s interior minister, Núria Parlon, said authorities do not plan to remove the housing-rights encampment in Plaça de Catalunya, arguing that it would be difficult to justify curtailing a protest over a problem affecting many people. The camp has grown since its first night, with protesters demanding stronger action on rents, evictions, homelessness and housing speculation. Organisers say the encampment may continue beyond Friday regardless of whether Spain’s proposed housing decrees are approved.
stories.headline: Catalan government says it will not clear Barcelona housing-rights encampment

stories.body: The trial of four Spanish National Police officers over activist Roger Español’s loss of an eye from a rubber bullet during the 2017 Catalan independence referendum entered its final day in Barcelona. Proceedings were briefly delayed after an accused inspector failed to appear, citing a sudden health problem, but resumed after he arrived with medical documentation. Prosecutors and civil-rights groups argue that evidence shows officers used rubber bullets unlawfully, while police testimony has maintained that the shot that injured Español may have ricocheted from the ground.
stories.headline: Trial over Roger Español’s loss of an eye during 2017 referendum reaches final day

stories.body: Changes to Spain’s general traffic regulations took effect, adding protections for vulnerable road users and new requirements for motorcyclists and electric-scooter users. Motorcyclists face rules on equipment including gloves on interurban roads and restrictions on riding in sandals or flip-flops, while the minimum age for electric scooters is set at 15. The changes also prohibit vehicle amber flashing lights from coinciding with a green pedestrian signal at traffic crossings, requiring municipalities to adjust incompatible signal sequences.
stories.headline: New Spanish traffic rules strengthen protections for motorcyclists, pedestrians and scooter users
